buffer: 25 mM deuterated HEPES, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3
construct_or_mutation: human p38γ (MAPK12, UniProt P53778), non-phosphorylated; the paper does not state whether NMR samples were full-length or p38γ(7–352)
other_conditions: 200-300 µM protein in 90%/10% H2O/D2O; related structures: 1CM8 (activated p38γ crystal structure), 1ERK and 2B9F (ERK2 and Fus3, other MAPKs with DFG pucker), 6UNA (this paper's apo crystal structure, open and compact molecules); regime (authors): fast exchange limit (kex > Δω_C), so phi_1/2 = (pA pB Δω_C^2)^1/2 reported instead of pB and Δω; Δω_H fixed to 0; CPMG block 20 ms; 15 methyl groups fit the global process; Met182, Leu225, Met262 fit individually; Met81 shows no dispersion; Leu77-δ1 and Ile149-δ report on DFG loop and HRD/αC configuration
timescale: kex = 960 ±30 s −1 (global two-site fit of 15 methyl probes); kex = 690 (10) s −1 (Met182-ε), 660 (60) s −1 (Leu225-δ1), 560 (40) s −1 (Met262-ε) (individual fits)
alt_state_structure: 6UNA: compact (active-like) molecule of the crystal, taken by the authors as representative of the weakly populated excited state; the open molecule represents the ground state (Discussion, Conformational fluctuations between open and compact structures; chains not specified in the text)
caveat_note: The card lists 293 K and 500/800 MHz; this row is methyl dispersion at 283 K and pH 7.2, not the 15N relaxation at 293 K and pH 6.8. The population pB and Δω_C are not separately determined because exchange is fast; the excited state is identified with the compact crystal molecule only through the correlation of predicted and fitted shift differences (R = 0.84), which the authors call strong but not proof. Per-residue Rex and phi_1/2 values are in Table 1 and Tables S4-S5, whose column layout is garbled in the text, so they are not transcribed.
experiment: multiple-quantum 13C-1H methyl CPMG relaxation dispersion (ILV and Met methyls, MILV 13C-labeled, perdeuterated) at 500 and 800 MHz, two-site Bloch-McConnell global fit (GLOVE)
author_claim: Inactive apo p38γ exchanges on the ms timescale between an open ground state and a weakly populated compact, active-like excited state; predicted shift differences between open and compact crystal molecules correlate with phi_1/2 (R = 0.84).
anchor: the data can be fit to a global exchange rate of 960 ±30 s −1
locator: Results, Exchange between open and compact states measured by methyl relaxation dispersion; Table 1; Discussion; conditions: Materials and Methods, Sample preparation and NMR spectroscopy

buffer: 25 mM deuterated HEPES, 250 mM NaCl, 1 mM TCEP, 0.01% w/v NaN3
ligand_or_partner: BIRB796 (DFG-out inhibitor), 2-fold molar excess, about 0.3% residual DMSO
construct_or_mutation: human p38γ (MAPK12, UniProt P53778), non-phosphorylated; the paper does not state whether NMR samples were full-length or p38γ(7–352)
other_conditions: 200-300 µM protein in 90%/10% H2O/D2O; related structures: 1CM8 (activated p38γ crystal structure), 1ERK and 2B9F (ERK2 and Fus3, other MAPKs with DFG pucker), 6UNA (this paper's apo crystal structure, open and compact molecules); DMSO control: two-point dispersion showed no difference with equivalent DMSO; two clusters of methyls with different kex; Leu77, Met109, Ile169 lose dispersion near the inhibitor site with large increases in R20; decreased dispersion for Ile149, Met182, Ile209, Leu265, Leu294
timescale: kex = 1900 s −1 (±70) (C-lobe cluster); kex = 310 s −1 (±60) (docking-site cluster: Met120, Leu119-δ2, Met219) (two-site fits per cluster)
caveat_note: Inhibitor-bound sample, not the apo deposit. The temperature 293 K is inferred from the comparison with apo 293 K in the same sentence; the paper does not give the BIRB796 temperature separately. Cluster membership beyond the named residues is in the supplement. Ligand binding itself also changes chemical shifts, so loss of dispersion may reflect altered Δω as well as altered dynamics.
experiment: multiple-quantum 13C-1H methyl CPMG relaxation dispersion at 500 and 800 MHz, two-site fit, BIRB796-bound p38γ
author_claim: Binding the DFG-out inhibitor splits the global ms process into a C-lobe process (kex 1900 s-1) and a slower docking-site process (kex 310 s-1), which the authors read as decoupling of motions by loss of the DFG pucker.
anchor: One corresponds to the previously described global fluctuation, but for a smaller cohort of residues within the C-lobe and with a slightly decreased exchange rate of 1900 s −1 (±70)
locator: Results, Exchange between open and compact states measured by methyl relaxation dispersion; Figure S8, Table S7 (supplement not available)

construct_or_mutation: p38γ(7–352) with a spontaneous Gln31/Arg mutation, N-terminal His6 tag removed by thrombin
other_conditions: crystallized by sitting drop vapor diffusion at room temperature; N-terminal β-strand swap between the two molecules; N-lobe pivots about hinge residues 111-114; Lys56-Asp153 distance decreased by 2.4 Å in the compact molecule; Asp171 shows two χ1 rotamers in the compact molecule; related structures: 1CM8
alt_state_structure: 6UNA: open (canonical inactive) and compact (active-like) molecules in the asymmetric unit, ground and excited-state analogs (Results, Crystal structure of inactive apo p38γ; chains not specified in the text)
caveat_note: Crystal structure of a truncated construct with a spontaneous Q31R mutation, not the solution sample. The domain swap and the lattice may influence the two molecules, although the authors report similar crystal contacts. Crystallographic temperature is not stated in the text. The compact state is a crystallographic state; its identity with the NMR excited state is inferred from shift correlations (R = 0.84).
experiment: X-ray crystal structure at 2.55 Å resolution; two molecules in the asymmetric unit compared with activated p38γ (1CM8)
author_claim: The crystal contains an open inactive molecule and a compact molecule intermediate between the inactive open state and the activated state; the compact molecule samples both inactive and active-like DFG loop conformations.
anchor: the two conformations in our p38γ crystal structure represent the canonical, open inactive apo state and a more compact state that is closer to the activated conformation
locator: Results, Crystal structure of inactive apo p38γ; Data Deposition; Figures 2 and 3
